demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Domestic steel demand is estimated to have grown by around 8%-10% during FY2025-26, driven by robust infrastructure development, construction activity and expanding manufacturing.
- Government-led infrastructure projects, including the Gati Shakti plan and PLI schemes, continued to provide sustained support to key steel-consuming sectors such as infrastructure, construction, railways and manufacturing.
- Sustained government capital expenditure, a busy construction season, and continued private investment in capacity expansion (including large integrated steel plants and value-added product lines) are expected to drive volume growth in the steel industry through FY2026-27.
- Rising investments in green/specialty steel, data centre infrastructure, defence manufacturing and shipbuilding are emerging as new demand drivers for the sector.
- Global steel demand growth remains modest, constrained by surplus capacity and weaker consumption in China and major Western economies, which continues to exert downward pressure on international steel prices and industry profitability.
- Domestically, rising imports and cost pressures could weigh on margins even as demand growth remains healthy.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The Singapore subsidiary, Readymade Steel Singapore Pte Ltd., continues to be under liquidation process; the Company has already impaired its investments and loan outstanding in this subsidiary.
- The material step-down subsidiary at Singapore (KH Foges Pte. Ltd.) is under Judicial Management / a scheme of arrangement (Resolution), and its financial figures are not available for consolidation.
- Accumulated losses in previous years have resulted in erosion of the Company's net worth, which remained negative in both FY2025-26 and FY2024-25.
- The Company has been facing hurdles over the last few years due to liquidity mismatch and continues to work with lenders towards a long-term viable resolution with its financial creditors.
- Persistent global steel overcapacity and weaker consumption in China and major Western economies exert downward pressure on international steel prices and industry profitability.
- Domestically, rising imports and cost pressures could weigh on margins even as demand growth remains healthy; the Company is also exposed to commodity price risk and foreign-currency exchange-rate risk on imports and export revenue.
- The economic environment remains complex, with risks stemming from geopolitical tensions and volatility in raw material and energy prices, which could affect global growth and trade flows.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- The Company continues to work with its lenders towards a long-term viable resolution of financial-creditor issues, supported by the preferential allotment of equity/warrants to strengthen its capital base.
- There was no change in the nature of business of the Company during the year under review.
